reachable: The mechanism is reachable in training and is genuinely active; it is structurally absent at scoring. Training: evolve/harness.py calls G.load_batcher(genome)(fit_stripped, bs, seed) and uses the returned list purely as `[fit_stripped[i] for i in idx]`, so every batch composition decision does shape the r22 in-batch loss. The objective r22_exact_target_equivalence_quotient flattens every cmd position of every sequence in the batch into one row set (pred, tgt = cmd_pred[m], tgt_full[m]) and makes every other row's target a candidate, so co-batched board-matched sequences really do become negatives for each other's read rows — the hypothesis's "~1900 rows" is consistent (64 seqs x ~30 cmd positions). The claimed selectivity is measured and real: board-matched-and-role-DIFFERING in-batch pair mass rises 0.019 -> 0.086 late in training while board-matched-and-role-SAME mass FALLS 0.021 -> 0.017, i.e. the round-robin over distinct role keys is doing exactly what it says rather than just clustering. Failure mode 1 (bucket sparsity), which the author could not test, does not bite: on the real split there are 93 board buckets, 87 with >=2 members, 68 with >=2 role keys, 39 with >=12 members. Scoring: no batcher is invoked anywhere in evolve/cups_probe.py, evolve/cups_ca.py, evolve/cdh_probe.py or eval/adapter.py (grep for load_batcher/next_batch returns nothing), so nothing this module computes can reach a scored prediction.
solves_outside_model: No violation. The symbolic replay resolves the move chain in Python, but its only output is a list of integer indices into `fit`. I verified by instrumentation, not by reading: wrapping each seq dict in a spy that records key access and running 49 batches, the only keys the batcher ever touches are ['cmds', 'image'] — never z_obs, never z_cmd, never ok. The module imports only math, re and torch, writes nothing, and mutates nothing (fit byte-identical after a full run). The resolved routing never becomes a token, a target or a scoring input; it selects SAMPLES, which the brief explicitly permits, and it is the same family of thing both parents already do. Contract checks all pass on the real split: exactly bs indices for bs in {8, 64, 960, 1000}, in range, all distinct when n >= bs, bit-identical across repeat runs with the same seed, different under a different seed, unchanged when the global torch/random RNGs are perturbed between calls (private generator throughout — every randperm/randint/rand/multinomial passes generator=g). Cost is negligible: 0.09s setup, 0.86s for 2000 next_batch calls.
summary: The code implements the hypothesis. The BOARD/ROLE split is exactly as described — BOARD = (n movers, n moves in window, window max hop count, digit-normalized 3-component root + arity of the read path), ROLE = (read thread's own hop count, birth rank among movers, first-mover flag) — and the swap-invariance argument holds: a role swap preserves the hop-count multiset (so max depth), the board and the read location, while permuting own-depth, birth rank and who opened. Buckets key on BOARD alone and members are drawn round-robin across distinct ROLE keys, and this is not just aspirational: measured on the real 2560-sequence training split, board-matched-role-DIFFERING in-batch pair mass rises 4.5x over uniform (0.019 -> 0.086) while board-matched-SAME-role mass falls, which is precisely the selectivity claimed. The bucket-sparsity failure mode the author flagged as untestable from the jail does not occur. The batcher is clean on the outside-the-model question — verified by key-access instrumentation, it reads only `cmds` and `image`, and no probe or the CA module ever constructs a batcher. Four divergences, all minor. The one that matters for the archive is a stated measured number that is false: "agree with the withheld generator metadata on every one of the 24" is actually 19/24 — though the two examples cited by name are both exactly correct, and every disagreement sits at generator depth 1-2, outside the eligible slice (within depths 3-4 it is 9/9 on the sample and 97.2% on the real split). "Exact epoch coverage" is likewise overstated: hard-block picks bypass the permutation cursor and colliding draws are silently dropped, and measured exposure runs 21..866 per sequence over 2000 steps. Separately worth recording beside the score, though not a claim/code contradiction: the inherited exp(0.8*depth) bucket tilt over-samples depth-5/6 boards that are outside the scored slice, so eligible-depth exposure share is 0.359 vs 0.371 under uniform and the enrichment inside the scored slice is 1.9x rather than the headline 4.5x. Nothing about comp_ca was checked — no training was run, by me or by the author, and my bucket/enrichment measurements are on one real root, not on the blend spec cloud/build_context.py composes at load time. I also did not verify that the r22 ring/importance weighting actually promotes board-matched read rows to dominant negatives (only that all rows are candidates), nor whether the three chosen role axes match the model's actual shortcut — the author's own failure mode 4.

divergences.claim: "Checked against evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl (24 real training trajectories): the tracker's recovered move count and window depth agree with the withheld generator metadata on every one of the 24."
divergences.what_the_code_does: It agrees on 19/24, not 24/24. Running _profile over all 24 jail samples and comparing (movers, moves, max-depth) against each row's withheld meta.cups {movers, R, depth}: rows 1,2,3,4,7,9,10,11,12,13,15,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,23 match; rows 0,5,6,8,14 do not. Rows 0/5/6/8: the tracker's deepest window is a cvar group, not the cups chain (recovered e.g. (3,3,2) vs gt (2,2,1)). Row 14: same window, but recovered depth 6 vs gt depth 2 — the generator's 'depth' is the ROUTED thread's depth, the impl's board depth is the window maximum, and row 14 is the case where those differ (depths {'1':6,'0':2}, routed_idx 0). The two examples the author cites by name (seq 3 -> 8 moves/depth 5/2 movers; seq 22 -> 8 moves/depth 4/3 movers) are both exactly right, so a real check was run; the universal quantifier is the overstatement. Mitigating: all five disagreements sit at generator depth 1-2, outside the eligible slice. Restricted to the eligible depths {3,4} the 24-sample check is 9/9, and on the real split (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl, 2560 sequences) the tracker recovers the cups window on 923/950 = 97.2% of eligible-depth sequences (68.4% over all depths, where cvar groups often out-depth a shallow cups chain).
divergences.evidence: Ran evolve/chunks/batcher/r5_board_matched_role_contrast_blocks.py::_profile over all 24 rows of evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl and over all 2560 rows of /Users/fanzhu/PyCharmProjects/terminal-wm/data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd/train.jsonl, comparing to meta.cups {movers, R, depth}. Counts: overall (movers,moves) match 1750/2560; incl. depth 1593/2560; eligible-depth subset 923 match / 27 mismatch.

divergences.claim: "the uniform remainder of every batch is drawn WITHOUT replacement from a reshuffled permutation ... Under a fixed step budget this gives exact epoch coverage."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The remainder is indeed drawn from a torch.randperm cursor (draw_uniform, lines 234-240), so the narrow half of the claim is true. "Exact epoch coverage" is not: hard-block picks (48 of 64 slots late in training) bypass the cursor entirely, and in the fill loop a permutation entry that collides with `used` is consumed and discarded (`v = draw_uniform(); if distinct and v in used: continue`), so it is dropped from that epoch. Measured over 2000 steps on the real split, per-sequence exposure counts run from 21 to 866 (median 38) — the top 1% of sequences absorb 10.4% of all training exposures. Coverage is complete (all 2560 seen) but nowhere near uniform.
divergences.evidence: Instrumented next_batch over 2000 steps, bs=64, genome params: distinct sequences seen 2560/2560; top-10 exposure counts [866, 853, 701, 639, 626, 618, 593, 584, 563, 522]; median 38; min 21.

divergences.claim: "one trajectory (which contains several independent groups — a cups mv chain plus several cvar accumulator groups) splits into connected windows" — i.e. the cups chain is one window.
divergences.what_the_code_does: _components unions threads only through shared directories, so a cups board whose two mover chains never touch a common directory splits into two windows, and the board key then describes a sub-board. Example, train.jsonl seq 277: generator board is 2 movers / R=6 / depth 4, but the backup.job chain never shares a directory with the f431->root.msg chain, so the recovered board is (1 mover, 4 moves, depth 4). This happens on 27 of the 950 eligible-depth sequences (~2.8%). The author's failure mode 5 anticipated the opposite error (windows merging), not splitting.
divergences.evidence: Printed the full command list and recovered profile for train.jsonl seqs 6, 70, 277 — each an eligible-depth case where recovered movers=1 while meta.cups movers has 2 entries.

divergences.claim: "Bucket choice is tilted toward deeper hop counts" combined with "Training pressure that specifically penalizes both of those [location-keyed and position-keyed predictors]" as the route to moving comp_ca.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The tilt is implemented exactly as stated (exp(depth_beta*deepest) * size^size_pow * n_roles^role_pow), but because the eligible slice is depths 3 and 4 ONLY, exp(0.8*d) with d capped at 6 spends a large share of the hard budget outside the scored slice. Measured: late-training board-depth histogram of selected sequences is {1:635, 2:748, 3:821, 4:591, 5:262, 6:847} against a uniform {1:3432, 2:3476, 3:3014, 4:2220, 5:381, 6:277} — depth-6 boards are ~3x over-represented although only 59 sequences carry one. Net effect on the scored slice: eligible-depth exposure share 0.359 vs 0.371 under uniform, i.e. slightly NEGATIVE. Consequently the headline enrichment of board-matched role-differing pair mass (0.019 -> 0.086, 4.5x) shrinks to 1.9x (0.088 -> 0.170) when restricted to pairs of eligible-depth sequences. This is inherited parent behavior the hypothesis explicitly says it kept, so it is not a claim/code contradiction — but it means the mechanism lands substantially weaker on the windows that are actually scored than the hypothesis reads.
divergences.evidence: Pairwise in-batch statistics over batches at steps 1500-1560 vs 200 uniform batches, plus exposure histograms over 2000 steps, on the real 2560-sequence train split.
